text:
anya: quick heads-up — during Venus v1 int8 bring-up we saw a consistent degradation on zh->en and mixed zh+ar inputs. small smoke numbers: BLEU -4.2, chrF -2.1 vs fp16 baseline. repro attached below.
hiro: thanks — is this across all prompts or specific to subtitle-style / vertical text?
anya: mostly short-form subtitle and UI labels. example: 
input: "【場景】用戶點擊"保存"後，提示: تم الحفظ بنجاح"
venus-int8: "[UNK] clicked save then prompt: تم الحفظ بنجاح"
venus-fp16: "[Scene] After the user clicks "Save", the prompt: Saved successfully"
sam: that looks like a tokenization / detokenization mismatch — the arabic phrase seems to be getting split/merged differently when the tokenizer map changes under quant kernels. any diffs in tokenizer artifacts between builds?
anya: tokenizer model hash is identical, but generated token boundaries differ on int8 runtime. I ran a tiny decode diff: token ids align until the CJK punctuation, then the int8 variant merges the following narrow arabic tokens (visible as single token id).
ml-eval-bot: automated-smoke: venus-v1 int8 vs fp16 small-1000-sample: BLEU_fp16=28.3, BLEU_int8=24.1, chrF_fp16=47.6, chrF_int8=45.5, samples_with_merge=112/1000. full CSV -> https://internal.redwood/evals/venus-int8-smoke.csv
hiro: ok can you paste the token id sequence for that example (both outputs)?
anya: pasted below: 
fp16 ids: 28901, 504, 4032, 110, 8, 22001, 3998
int8 ids: 28901, 504, 4032, 110, 82214
(note: 82214 is a fused id in the int8 runtime)
sam: that fused id is suspicious — likely kernel-level token remap happening in the quantized tokenizer op. which runtime kernel is used? nvapex-int8 or xla-optimized?
anya: nvapex-int8 on our Dedicated config. same model on hosted (xla-fused) shows a smaller gap (-1.3 BLEU) not -4.2.
kevin: so Hosted xla-fused still has merge but much smaller. Could be a codegen change in nvapex kernel that reorders subtoken merges for mixed-script contexts.
hiro: can we isolate by running tokenizer-only binary with the nvapex tokenizer op used in inference? run: ./venustools/tokenize --input-file repro.txt --use-kernel nvapex-int8 --dump-ids > ids_nv.txt; ./venustools/tokenize --input-file repro.txt --use-kernel fp16-ref --dump-ids > ids_fp.txt; diff ids_nv.txt ids_fp.txt
anya: ran that — diff shows the fused id only when using nvapex-int8. I also checked the kernel commit: kernel hash 3a7f1c changed merge heuristics (PR #4127).
sam: PR 4127 was meant to improve speed by collapsing zero-width joiner sequences, but sounds like it's overzealous for CJK+RTL adjacencies. can we add a quick patch to skip fusings across script-boundaries?
kevin: patch idea: in the kernel, add an additional check: if (script(prev_token) != script(next_token)) skip_fuse = true. cheap and should guard mixed-script cases.
hiro: please also add a focused unit test: mixed_cjk_arabic_fuse -> ensure no fusion. add to token-fuzz suite.
anya: created a tiny reproducer and test in repo: tests/mixed_script/fuse_regression_repro.txt -> contains the example above; git branch: fix/avoid-script-fuse-venus-4127
triage-bot: created ticket INF-1298 with logs and attached smoke CSV. assigned to @sam and @hiro.
sam: I'll prototype the patch and run smoke (1000 sample) locally. if numbers improve we can roll as nvapex hotfix.
kevin: if hotfix is risky, alternative is routing rule: for Dedicated only, fallback tokenizer op to fp16-ref for requests with mixed-script detection (cheap S-script heuristic at router). it's heavier but lower blast radius.
anya: agree — prefer kernel fix first, router fallback as short-term mitigation. I'll hold off on Dedicated rollout until we confirm.
hiro: next actions: sam -> patch + unit test + perf microbench (ensure fusion perf delta <5%), anya -> expand smoke to mixed zh+ar and zh+he sets, kevin -> prepare routing fallback PR if needed.
anya: tagging results here when smoke completes. thanks all :thumbsup: 
kevin: ping if you want me to run canary in one Dedicated pool.
sam: starting patch now, will update in thread.
